# Devices

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_device_catalog.py from rain_stats/constants.py. Do not edit by hand: run the tool. -->

The plugin creates the devices below. No unit number ever changes and no unit is ever reused, so an upgrade keeps every device, its history, scenes, scripts and schedules.

**Which windows get devices is your choice.** In the file `.env` beside `plugin.py` there is one line per window, `RS_LAST_001_DAYS=Y` ... `RS_LAST_365_DAYS=N`: `Y` creates the rain device of that window and its peak rain rate device, `N` creates neither. Without a `.env`, or without the line, the default of the table below is in force. A device that exists already is never deleted by the plugin: when you set `N` it stays where it is and is no longer updated (delete it in Domoticz when you do not want it any more). At least one window must be `Y`. Changes take effect when the hardware is restarted.

Every chosen device is created when missing (at start and at every poll) and *in use* from the start, so nothing has to be added by hand under Setup > Devices. All devices are read-only: a command sent to one is answered by writing its real value back.

## Status (units 17-18)

| Unit | Name | Type | Unit label | Source | Created when |
|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| 17 | Rain Stats Status | Switch (On/Off), read-only | - | the connection: On while the rain device can be read, Off while it cannot | always |
| 18 | Rain Stats Info | Text, read-only | - | the plugin: last reading, rain rate, since when data are collected, partial windows | always |

- **Rain Stats Status** follows the source: On while the rain device can be read, Off while it cannot. The statistics themselves never change because of a failed read: the windows keep sliding with the clock.
- **Rain Stats Info** is a short text, for example `OK 08:34: 0.0 mm/h; collecting since 2026-11-18 00:00; windows from 1d on are partial` or `Source not reachable since 08:12: the statistics go on from the stored data`. With an imported history it also says `history from 2025-11-21` and, when the rain windows are complete but the peak rates are not, `peaks from 1d on are partial`.

## The windows

Rain is stored in a round-robin archive: fixed rings of equally long time slots, reused in a circle. Nothing grows and nothing is trimmed; the slot that becomes too old is overwritten by the one that takes its place. Every reading is added to both tiers:

| Tier | Slot | Slots | Remembers | Answers |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| fine | 5 min | 2016 | 7 d | 1 d, 2 d, 7 d |
| coarse | 15 min | 35040 | 365 d | 14 d, 30 d, 60 d, 90 d, 120 d, 180 d, 360 d, 365 d |

The **rain** of a window is the last N hours or days: the slot that is running now, the slots before it that make up the window, and the part of the slot before those that still lies inside the period, in proportion (rain is taken to have fallen evenly within a slot; the rain rings keep one slot more than the table says, for that part). So a storm fades out of a window through one slot instead of dropping out in one step, and on average the window is neither too high nor too low. The **peak rate** cannot be taken in proportion: it is made of whole slots only, the running one plus the ones before it, so it covers between N-1 slots and N slots of real time and **never reaches further back than the name says**:

| Window | Tier (slot) | Slots | Rain covers | Peak rate covers | Devices | `.env` line | Default |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 d | fine (5 min) | 288 | the last 1 d | 23 h 55 min to 1 d | units 1 and 9 | `RS_LAST_001_DAYS` | Y |
| 2 d | fine (5 min) | 576 | the last 2 d | 47 h 55 min to 2 d | units 2 and 10 | `RS_LAST_002_DAYS` | Y |
| 7 d | fine (5 min) | 2016 | the last 7 d | 167 h 55 min to 7 d | units 3 and 11 | `RS_LAST_007_DAYS` | Y |
| 14 d | coarse (15 min) | 1344 | the last 14 d | 13 d 23 h 45 min to 14 d | units 4 and 12 | `RS_LAST_014_DAYS` | Y |
| 30 d | coarse (15 min) | 2880 | the last 30 d | 29 d 23 h 45 min to 30 d | units 5 and 13 | `RS_LAST_030_DAYS` | Y |
| 60 d | coarse (15 min) | 5760 | the last 60 d | 59 d 23 h 45 min to 60 d | units 19 and 22 | `RS_LAST_060_DAYS` | N |
| 90 d | coarse (15 min) | 8640 | the last 90 d | 89 d 23 h 45 min to 90 d | units 6 and 14 | `RS_LAST_090_DAYS` | Y |
| 120 d | coarse (15 min) | 11520 | the last 120 d | 119 d 23 h 45 min to 120 d | units 20 and 23 | `RS_LAST_120_DAYS` | N |
| 180 d | coarse (15 min) | 17280 | the last 180 d | 179 d 23 h 45 min to 180 d | units 7 and 15 | `RS_LAST_180_DAYS` | Y |
| 360 d | coarse (15 min) | 34560 | the last 360 d | 359 d 23 h 45 min to 360 d | units 21 and 24 | `RS_LAST_360_DAYS` | N |
| 365 d | coarse (15 min) | 35040 | the last 365 d | 364 d 23 h 45 min to 365 d | units 8 and 16 | `RS_LAST_365_DAYS` | Y |

- The windows slide with the clock: they are recomputed at least every 60 seconds and after every reading, so rain leaves a window while it is dry, without any new reading.
- A window is **partial** while the plugin knows less time than the window is long. Its value is the rain (or the peak) of the time that is known, never an estimate of the rest. The rain is known from the start of collecting, or from the start of the imported daily history when there is one (`RS_HISTORY_IDX`); the peak rain rate only from the start of collecting, because the history has no rates. *Rain Stats Info* names the first partial window.
- Values are written when they change and rewritten every 300 seconds when they do not, so Domoticz' sensor time-out never marks a quiet sensor as dead.
- Domoticz refuses new devices while *Setup > Settings > System > Accept new Hardware Devices* is off. The plugin says so once in the log and asks again every 5 minutes, so the devices appear as soon as the setting is on, without restarting the hardware.
- A name, a visibility or a unit label you set yourself in Domoticz is never overwritten; a sensor that was created without a unit label gets its unit at start.
